chapterTitle: Chapter 3: Synaptic Memoriam of a steel fossil shell
editorText:
"How long do you think it will take them to figure out the green room" Said John, looking over to Tebo. Tebo seemed unbothered, overcome with excitement for what lay ahead. "It served its purpose" he concluded. Doesn't matter "What's more important right now is this girls signature". Tebo paned through a series of burn plumes on the ships overhead display “There we are… standard export carrier plume for the exit region… check” The ships chaotic burn hummed and churned with strange sounds easing off to a once again steady less chaotic burn, "Can't hide from’em on an exit burns power draw, the cloak tech draws to much energy from the drive… may as well fool them!” Tebos visor lit up in what seemed like a smile as he turned back to the others. I've set our drive signature to match haulers in the region. By the time we come in visual range of the blockade, we can actuate our cloaking technology. Suddenly the violent vibrations through the ship simmered down to a soft hum. “We’ve just entered the stratosphere, Engines running silent. Electrical systems and vitals kept to a minimum. She’s cold."

Over in the co-pilot's seat, John seemed uneasy. He couldn't piece together how passing the Protectant blockade would be so easy. He knew Tor,  of his engineering prowess. “The Sparrow from our earlier encounter, Tau did you get a chance to pull it’s logs.. any outgoing transmissions about the Sentient cloaking tech it encountered on the ground? It won't take much for their sensors counter new tech, the engineers could have patched it. I would suggest setting cloak frequency to a different transform, they could be searching that frequency for anomalies”.  Tau looked in John’s direction" Since when did you take up my anxiety issues" John looked back at her then turned back looking up to his terminal. "Just a gut feeling”

“I get it, you’ve only been pulled out of the shit once by me..” Tebo joked sarcastically “The cloaking technology itself is different to that used in Earth’s atmosphere. I’ll remind you that sound doesn’t travel the same in space, well not at all.. Fooling light in space requires a more.. Physical disguising mechanism”. “It’s impressive” Said Tau, locking into her helmet left arm followed by her right. “Thanks lefty” Tebo remarked.

“It’s too quiet they should have hailed us by now, what’s the fucking hold up!” Tau seemed nervous like she had been on the observing end of the bridge before when others had been caught out trying to seek economical asylum in the belt from economic threshold sectors.

"I'm starting the vacuum preparations, I want hull breach measures at the ready" John concluded as he keyed his terminal into autopilot, raising it from around his shoulders over his head in one swift motion, The command console neatly tucking into the roof out of the way. He rose from his seat and moved toward the cargo hold with quick, calculated steps.

The others unstrapped from their G seats. Tau was first followed by Tex then Shai. They carried the weight of John’s judgment out like assumed orders without question or doubt, calmly making their way to the cargo hold where their freshly serviced and upgraded mark IV's waited. “Mark SP1” Tebo had termed his modifications.

Their boots clamped to the deck clanking one after the other. All was still and quiet as though they were all clanking around a floating tin can. John was the first to make it to his suit in the cargo hold wings splayed out with the others. I vats of the cargo hold had been supplied with the same gelatinous fluid that the suit's neuro-link jump suits synchronised with The suits all lined the cargo hold leant over like sleeping angels

John adjusted his suit and looked over at Tebo in the cockpit, calm as ever.

"You’re sure these signals are clean, right? Last thing we need is a surprise rail slug through the hull right now."

Tebo barely glanced up from the console, fingers tapping effortlessly. "Clean as they come. Focus on your vacuum prep. If anything does happen, we’ll be ready."

Tex grinned from the back, already locked in. The back of his suit reached around his back locking him in holding him up firmly. He was facing the outer hull, veering out the cloaked cargo hull, leaning against the wall. It almost seemed real. Tebo had coded the reflective transparent nano magnetic field of nanobots to reflect one micro panelled side to the onlookers.

“The cloaking technology itself is different to that used in Earth’s atmosphere. As you all know sound does not travel in space”. “It’s impressive” Said Tau, locking into her helmet left arm followed by her right. “Thanks lefty” Tebo remarked.

 When Tex veered out of the ship, an algorithm in his helmet rendered it almost seamless. As he veered through the cold shell of the helmets visor. They all took a moment to appreciate the difference in viewpoint through the helmet. Where the strangely reflected angles of the nanobots all but vanished from the close view point of the ships occupant within. When they put their heads into there helmets they felt at ease. Tau hoped that the Sentient technology was as good as he claimed it to be. She trusted Tebo’s confidence in the way he explained the technology. His voice strong and firm with rigour.

"Ain’t nothin’ ready for a railgun slug through the hull, though. You sure that fancy energy converter’s gonna save your hide if we spring a leak?" Tebo turned, unphased, raising an eyebrow. "if a slug hits the hull big guy, you'll be changing fuel cells before you have time to worry about my converter.", John interviened. “I’ll get the shells, Tex up top if it comes to that, I want you on the Rail gun support with Tebo if they open fire”.

Shai had just finished checking her bio gel reserves. “If you take a round big guy no sweat, just don’t get domed hey…. The logistics of getting in touch with your sleeve, isn’t really an option last I checked”. Tau gave a timeline of return, “Oasis is a long haul away from protectant jurisdiction according to Tebo, but the carrier get us there in time if anyone gets hurt fast enough”. John nodded to Tau then Tex pitched in with a smugness. “Marcellus I am sure would love to interrogate you if you tried jumping back in one of your sleeves”.

Tau smiled as though she was up to something as the words expired from Tex’s lips. "Well, that's comforting." John adjusted his helmet, his tone half-joking but his movements precise. "At least we won't be sucked through a pinhole, right?"

Tebo finally smirked, the closest he ever came to a joke. "No, John. Your guts will remain intact. All the equipment too. Just don’t take a round to the calf. I don’t know how useful you will be if your boots maglock cell takes a round, ever tried fighting in zero G?" John seemed confident, “Won’t be the first time” He cocked back the chamber on his Sherpa rifle, then checked the ammo reserve banks for his suit.

Tebo tuned back to his console, the faint hum of the vacuum system starting up. "And before you ask, yes—we’ll have enough air to get to the Jump ." Then pushed the vacuum handle on the cockpit to Active.

Tex chuckled as he locked his gear into place. "We don’t even know where we’re headed, but this guy's sure we'll have extra. I like that." John added in "Your only saying that because you’re not the one watching the gauges." Tebo, already back to scanning signals, gave a brief nod. "You worry too much, John. That's why I'm here, Sit back and enjoy the ride."

“We’ve reached Vacuum. We are approaching international space"Said Tau .The ship fell to the silent hum of the quantum fusion couple engine, awaiting it’s next vector thrust trajectories. By now they had all strapped into the holding bays in the cargo looking at one another in almost unison Tau Tex and Shai, closed their visors creating a crisp seal. Tebo, not being subject to the cold of vacuum went about his duties carefree. “All systems showing optimal guys, let's see if they accept our transit request”.

“It’s too quiet” said Tau, eyeing the time in her HUD. “10 seconds”, The others looked at each other in anticipation “Sorry just a delay in the translator” chuckled Tebo. Patching through the Hail now.

“Haul carrier X15-8901”. There was a moment of silence. Tebo engaged the microphone, although this time his voice was not himself. It was a female operator. “Copy Sky Dome, I have you loud and clear Haul Carrier X15-8901” over” another pause between radio static over the hangar bay, “copy that”, “One more thing X15..your load seems off”.,Tebo was fast in his respones “Copy  control, I think it’s just the glare from the sun, could be throwing out your video feeds volumetric calculations, give it some time to correct itself”

In the moment the soft feminine words left tebo’s emitter, the quantum couple of the light shield seemed to shrink inward momentarily, the light from the sun still piercing through like a blistering explosion. So much sound in the feeds of the protectants monitoring scanners didn’t allow precise measurements of the ship.

The voice of the global astreroid defence systems operator was softer, kinder. “Ahh yes, we have you at the correct load estimate and ship make. Welcome to Ceres Madam.. We have your departure papers leaving Ceres station tomorrow morning at 0600”, “Copy that Sky Dome, speak again at the transit  tomorrow

morning, have yourself a lovely evening”.

———————————————————————————————-

Meanwhile on the Balaenoptera.  an alarm flashed over Tors terminal froman algorithm he had implemented earlier to detect any discrepancies picked up over the chatter and volumetric scans at the planetary asteroid defence  on the sky dome Channel.

“Marcellus… we have a haul carrier requesting transit through to Ceres Station. The paperwork and logistics seem fine, but there’s a discrepancy in the ship volumetrics upon arriving at the transit .”

“What’s the callsign?” Said Marcellus, Tor frantically flicked the data over to the bridge monitors, displaying a hologram of the ship for Marcellus to examine.

“What are you hiding, X15-8901?” Marcellus muttered, pacing across to Tor’s terminal and standing at his side.

“The initial volumetric scans were off, but then they corrected again,” Tor explained.

“What was the light penetration from the sun? Did we get any interference?” Marcellus gleaned closer in at the Hauler.

“The scan was taken at 0800 hours, right on sun set.” Said Tor wiping a drip of sweat from his forehead.  “Hmm… what percentage were the volumetrics out?”, “Two percent, sir.” Tor shot back. “I see. That’s not uncommon around that time of day. And when they cleared the , did the scans correct?” “Yes, sir.” “Then what are you flagging it for?”

“Sir… I deemed it necessary with the heightened security measures.” Tors words trembled for a moment as they left his lips.

“Hmm. I see. Fair call, Lieutenant.” Tor sighed relaxing a bit more dropping his shoulders slightly.

Marcellus leaned closer to the monitor, his eyes narrowing. “Zoom in on that ship from the previous scan.” Tor got back into action lifting his shoulders immediately in response to Marcellus’s order. his hands twisted, angling the ship’s hologram to a narrower viewpoint looking along the cockpit window back to the engines. Then, with a spreading gesture, he zoomed in on the model. The image, reconstructed from 32 scan viewpoints, displayed reasonable clarity. A small amount of glare could be seen on the hologram from the sensors facing the sun, scattering any distinguishable details.

“Zoom in on the shaded side of the vessel,” Marcellus ordered. “Focus on the cockpit.” Tor complied, adjusting the view. “Sir… the cockpit windows,” Tor hesitated, his brow furrowing. “They seem to have some static in the image. I can’t make out the pilot.”

Marcellus’s jaw tightened as he stared at the display. “Something’s off. I want you to intercept that hauler and redirect them to the nearest inspection bay. Get a lock on them immediately as a warning if they decide to try anything funny”, “Putting it through, Commander,” Tor replied, his fingers dancing across the terminal. Tor rested his hand on his Chin prying gazing deeper into the haul carriers call sign “X15-8901??” He pondered. Then his gaze broke. A blue strobe accompanied message notification hovered across the Cockpit “Earth Secretary General Lady Ava Meerakavita requesting call to the bridge” Marcellus queased at the notification “Gahh dam Technocrats, put her through Tor!”

The screens hanging above the bulkheads of the bridge brought up a video feed of the Earth General Secretary for Defence, her perspective overlooking the operations table and the countless engineers and ranking officers of the bridge. They bowed their heads in respect.

“Lady Ava, what graces us with your timely presence?” Marcellus seemed enthusiastic initially, erring off to contempt and lethargy, like he could only afford her so much energy in the immediate urgency of the situation.

Lady Ava was enough—a still patience in her tone, but it was underlined with a mutual annoyance. “Would you care to update me on the most recent developments, Marcellus? Why are we firing Electron-class missiles and then target locking with warheads without my prior authorisation? I already have a political shitstorm on my hands from the previous ordnance disposed of over the lost facility.

It’s still unclear what exactly it is you claim you were shooting at—no evidence of any rogue sentient activity. Your data that was sent to my office is incomprehensible.”

Marcellus sighed, “We felt it to be necessary considering the circumstances surrounding the last outbreak of rogue code at the facility, in order to contain any malicious codes that might otherwise infest or compromise our own system integrity. John and his team knew the details. They knew the risks associated if they meddled with old compromised systems.”

“That may be so, Marcellus, but aren’t you curious to at least attempt to contain this so-called outbreak in a manner which values the lives of your loyal men and women that have placed their lives on the line to investigate this apparent threat?

It seems the only threat to human life at this moment as I see it are us, in the eyes of certain parties… well… I can’t entirely agree with your methods.”

———————————————————————————————-

Back on the Beverly, Tebo was deep into his checks, syncing the ship’s  operations, when Kitten interrupted his focus.

“Tebo, my friend,” Kitten began, leaning casually against a terminal. “How’d you know the glare would buy us time?”

“Just enough time, my friend,” Tebo replied, not even looking up. His fingers flew across the console, his focus unwavering.

John hovered nearby, uneasy. The others had relaxed, already breaking into quiet chatter, celebrating the easy slip past the Haul inspection bay. Whatever Tebo had planned next, it seemed to them like smooth sailing—or at least, for now.

“What do you think it’s like out there?” Shai asked, her voice soft as she retracted her visor back into her helmet. Her gaze shifted to Tau, curiosity in her tone. “I don’t know,” Tau replied, her visor sliding back with a soft hiss. “Better, I hope.”

John glanced over his shoulder at them before returning his attention to the terminals. Beside him, Tebo was immersed in priming the Quantum Lock Fusion Drive for a full burn. From his forearm extended a lattice of translucent wires, intertwining seamlessly with the terminal's input ports, like the delicate roots of a tree seeking connection.

The light coursing through those threads pulsed with an almost ethereal glow, each surge alive with intent. What at first appeared rhythmic gave way to a deliberate, almost sentient pattern—each flicker and shift of energy a step in a complex, unseen choreography. The terminal responded in kind, its interface lighting up in a series of cascading hues, echoing Tebo’s precision.

It was more than input; it was symbiosis. Every motion of Tebo’s mechanical limbs seemed less like a command and more like a conversation between the machine and its master, his movements fluid yet purposeful. The terminal's soft hum harmonised with the faint crackle of energy as if both were breathing in unison.

Something had shifted, the pattern now erratic yet purposeful, as if the Tebo itself were bracing the ship for evasive maneouvers. John’s voice cut through the cargo hold, amplified by the PA. “Visors down!”

The authority in his tone sent a ripple through the crew. Tau and Shai reacted instantly, their visors snapping back into place. Tex just shrugged, his still securely affixed.

Tebo smirked slightly, his hands never pausing just patiently observing unease between the others. “Buckle up, kids. Things are about to get interesting.” Tex chuckled to himself. The ship had shifted. Tebo had reorented the ship facing directly for the sun, the cockpit of the Beverly exploded with hot light, as the Suns rays blinded John momentarily as his visors light sensors struggled to keep up with the sudden influx.

Shai held onto her bay cradles nervously strapping into the High G burn seat. Tex and Tau following suit. Silence broke yet again the same familiar  controller voice over the ship speakers. “Cargo Hauler X15-8901 You are to return to the inspection bay immediately, Do not alter your trajectory course. Continue onto” Tebo interrupted the call over the radio “Copy that  Control, We appear to be experiencing control system failure, can you please send help” Tebo exchanged a cheeky smile with John tilting his head in his direction. Continuing on his set trajectory “What the fuck are you doing Tebo.. They’re about to lock on us if we don’t turn tail and head to that bay we will be space showers for the next Hauler..” John added cautiosly and more calmly after “We aren’t gunned for this fight..” John’s voice croaked with anticipation at Tebo’s next move. “Yes the Beverly isn’t gunned for a full assault, but that’s not what we’re doing my friend, don’t worry I have a trick up my sleeve, it’s allll in the simulation”. John calmed himself Tau and Shai following his aura. “If you say so, Tau get me up rear defence sectors, and about face the rail cannon on our Tail so we can use the discharge force to aid our Escape, Tex I want you on rail gunner, Tau Shai Port and starboard PDC’s respectively, me and Tebo will handle the bowel”, “Copy that” Said Tau, “Gahh I always take the bigseat” chuckled Tex. “Your the only one that fits in the darn thing” laughed John. The atmosphere eased for a moment now with John asserting direction.

“Johnn.. ” Tau seemed uneasy in her voice. “They have us locked, Electron Fusion Class Engine Missiles, we can’t outlast those kind of speeds and burn times, we will have to engage if they fire” “Hmmm silent, and fast” Tebo still seemed unphased by the apparent and imminent danger of the situation. The radio hailed once more “X15-8901 Change trajectory, this is you final 5 second warning, we are unable to assist at present, Kill your burn and await recovery, You have 5 seconds to comply”. “Of course Controller, I have you loud and clear, commencing burn cool down sequence”. John could tell the little machine man was simply trying to buy them as much time, he knew that they could not outrun missiles, He also knew they could atleast make it difficult for a rail cannon intercept  The more distance he put between them as possible.

The cockpit of the Beverly lit up in a pulsing amber and red transition. “Incoming Missile detected” pulsed in Red, “Missile Lock”, Amber. shot across the bulkhead emergency displays. The red and amber flick creating an eery anticipation in the cargo hold, yet at the front of the ship John and Tau seemed focused, determined, almost as much as Tau. “That cruise missile will reach us in 2 minutes if we don’t intercept or comply”. Tau was already mounting her defence setting firing vectors for the storm rail cannon mounted just behind the cockpit of the Beverly.

She looked over to Tex “I hope you ran your checks thoroughly " . "Smooth as a whistle. Tex replied confidently." Kitten chimed in pleasantly as always." I have created a firing sequence for you miss Vang " . Tex had just loaded and primed the storm rail"thankyon kitten" Then began climbing up into the pilot seat of the rail cannon"do you think this old girl will have enough 'charge to keep them at that range?", The Storm rail 1st guns are reliable enough. "And the new cells we updated the Bev with will go beyond parameters you humies are used to" Said Tebo

"He means to say it will work" said Tex. Pulling down the aiming visor of the cannon into his sites "how many of these fish do we have to pop" Said Tex. Tau frantically checked her HUD once again “One so far, we need to keep our eyes peeled. as there could be more coming. be ready" Kitten interrupted Tau "The first missile is coming into range". As soon as she spoke the Storm rail could be heard charging up. It's internal armature loading a slug into place. “Machine Man.. I’m only at 60% charge”

Kitten continued to announce."First missile intercept in 10 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4,.." “Tebooo” Croaked Tex his sites locked directly on the missiles nose brief silence John watched Tebo, completely unphased.

————————————————————————————

2097 Earth Outer Orbit.

Marcellus watched on from the bridge on the Balaenoptera, the missiles data feed showing the Ice Haulers thrust plume edging closer, brighter until there was nothing but crackled static spewing colours and then the dark void of space complimented by a blinding sun. No ship debris, No camera feed connection loss, It appeared like from the camera feed as though the missile had been teleported, past the hauler. “What in the hell happened, where are they on the Radar, No confirmed hit, but no Hauler, what the hell is going on down their Lieutenant” Marcellus whipped his word around the bridge like he was herding cattle. “Sir, that ship it just changed shape”, “How is that even possible?”, “I’m not sure but I am pretty sure when we last checked we weren't hailing a science research vessel” “What in tarnation” Marcellus gleaned closer on the periscope fix of what was once Cargo Hauler X15-8901. It certainly wasn’t a cargo hauler anymore. “That ship didn’t change shape Tor, It’s dam cloaking technology, and something we’ve never intercepted before.. over half a century ago”

“Lady Ava, Do you recognize this Vessel?” Marcellus zoomed in on the Beverly, a moment he allowed her to recall. “I Recall a certain Engineer who enticed in extraterrestrial initiatives through her work, Not approved of course by your Technocrats, off target? Wouldn’t I be within reasonable force to lets say decommission that project rightfully”

“And the people flying that ship Marcellus, what have they done to you”, “Insubordination of a clear directive?”, “So they should be court marshalled, not blown to oblivion?” Ava rebutted, “Well that would be so, however do you see those PDC’s… and the storm rail mounted on it’s hull. This is not a scientific vessel anymore, it’s a direct threat to the lives and souls on Ceres station, we have an obligation to deter and defend at all costs the lives of those on that station wouldn’t you agree”

“John.. What have you gotten yourself into” Ava muttered under her voice with deep concern, but only so loud that Marcellus and the bridge officers could only just guess the name.  “And tell me Commander, when that new sleeve comes off the ice, how do you think he will feel knowing how his predecessor met his end” Lady Ava recognised the name of the vessel, John’s horse from when he had grown up, as much as John could not remember entirely given his conditioning, Ava appreciated the deep meaning his mother had emblazoned the ship with in her discrete naming.

“What better way to set an example of what happens when you stray from a directive” Marcellus smirked then carried on wi thout waiting for Ava’s response “Tor what are the lifescan readings you are picking up on that vessel. That name on the vessel… I don’t recognise it”. Tor staggered immediately into action pressing keys upon his terminal to access the  scan data. “Loading up life-form scan data now sir” The screen pulsed a loading symbol as the ships acoustic listeners also homed in on the Beverly’s location. “Sir it’s it’s showing.. 4 Human lifeforms, and one.. Well it doesn’t seem to show up like anything on our register, it appears, machine, like an operating system of sorts, I can’t tell if it is part of the ships internal control system or another individual unit, the code certainly is unlike anything I have seen before..” Without hesitation Marcellus snided in his remark “Send everything we have, waves of 8. I want that vessel erased from the history books”

———————————————————————————————-

The cockpit of the Beverly lit up with the softer now yellow caution status, “Aren’t we meant to be dust right now” Said Shai, “That electron class cruise missile.. It’s “Tau gleaned closer into her Terminal” It’s turning around.. It went straight past us? I don’t get it!" “Warning shots are always targeted at the outer burners to cripple and preserve life, instead of completely taking out the main burner and leaving potential for life support failure.. It’s standard operating procedure” Said John.

“John’s correct” continued Tebo “They hit what they thought was our port aft burner, but it was just a light illusion created by the quantum light couple cloak”

Tau looked up at Tebo, who was confidently perched in his cockpit chair. “They rely heavily on image processing because of the glare zone… Tebo, you’re a genius! They didn’t have the capability to focus on heat signatures because of the interference caused by the sun!”

Tebo turned back and smiled. “We’re not out of the clear yet. Now our cover’s blown, I’m redirect the energy from the cloaking shield to full burn on our thrusters.” His connection with the terminal lit up once more, the pulses of light more erratic than before, like a storm trapped within the wires.

“What about the dummy cargo? Should we ditch that too, seeing as our cover’s blown?” John asked, his tone cautious.

Tebo smirked. “It may still prove useful.”

“I hope you’re right,” John replied, glancing at the sensors. “We’ve got eight missiles incoming—warhead class 4—and that EMP missile? It’s headed straight back for us.”

Tex grunted, adjusting his weapons console. “I’ve got the warheads in my sights. Someone do something about that EMP missile !”

Tebo’s calm voice suddenly filled the comms. “Buckle in—we’re about to pull some serious G’s.”

The plume of the Beverly didn’t erupt in flames but unfurled with precision, like the opening of a flower. The ship roared forward, its thrust perfectly controlled and deliberate.

Tex, Shai, Tau, and John groaned as their bodies strained against the intense G-forces.“Four G’s and rising,” John croaked, his voice tight as he struggled to breathe.“We’re about to get hit with a cocktail of adrenaline and stabilisers,” Shai added, bracing herself. “Sit back and enjoy the ride.” Said Tex like he had just opened his first beer for the night.

The ship propelled forward at a breakneck pace, closing the gap with the cruise missile that had turned back toward them. Onboard the electron class cruise missile, Tor watched on from the Bealenoptera, the Beverly’s cockpit grew larger on his monitor with every passing moment, his expression frozen in disbelief at what he was watching. Ava gasped in astonishment.

“It’s suicide!” Tau exclaimed, panic creeping into her voice. “We’ll be sitting ducks if that thing fries our engine controls!”, “Prepare to brace, comrades,” Tebo said calmly. Then, without warning, he fell silent, his glowing head tilting slightly forward, as though he’d entered a trance.

“What the faark?” Shai muttered sarcastically, her eyes darting toward Tau with concern written across her face. Tau’s lip curled slightly, but she said nothing. Suddenly, the burn eased, and the Beverly came to a standstill.

The rhythmic pulses of energy that had been flowing from Tebo into the terminal had now reversed direction, coursing back into him. The lights across his visor rippled and flickered with a strange, hypnotic pattern.

“Did we just cop an EMP hit?” John asked, confusion colouring his tone as he scanned the terminal. “All systems are still operational!” Tau replied, her voice matching his urgency. Her gaze shot to Tebo, who remained in his meditative state.

Slowly, he leaned forward, the glow of his head intensifying. Ripples formed across his visor, radiating outward like electrical waves. With a subtle shockwave that amplified from the nose of the Beverly, the incoming missile’s plume flickered and died.

The missile floated lifelessly in the void, its thrust extinguished—a useless hunk of electronics adrift in space. Tebo re-engaged the thrusters to full blast. The missile, now just a dead cylinder, bounced harmlessly off the Beverly’s nose like a discarded soda can.“Okay… that’s a new trick,” John quipped, his voice light despite the tension. Tebo turned to the left his glance fixed on John. His visor swirled with comical patterns. “space junk now,” he shrugged seeming to grin.

The missile flickered and spat about as the electron pulse plasma plume seemed to strangle what remained of it’s banks uncontrollably. Tebo began to cite information from his play book. “The doctor injected a day 0 code within the manufacturing the missile systems, the code will now drain any reserve in the missile to lame it in case of recovery”.

Tebo's theatrics were merely compliment to the already planned dropout of the missile. "Day Zero code" Tebo said smoothly "The Dr sure has his methods” Tex paused for a moment "Hmm" Sighed, and glanced at the missiles that had been tailing them getting closer and closer. The Beverlys’s plume burst out into a full burn thrust. The shroud of the now disposed missile slipped into the shadow of a planetary defence cannon. "Hey Cap, Do we need to be worried about those rock killers?" Tex seemed a little concerned watching it shell get tossed into the side of the cannon’s floating mass.

John looked over to Tebo, Tebo seemed care free, not even concerned with the question, John shrugged looking at Tex. Kitten broke the silence like a letter opener spilling out information in what she felt would calm and focus them.

"As far as i know planetary defence systems are not authorised for engagements where human life is at play, due to the Calibre of the rail systems engagements may also result in higher casualties due to unplanned solar fallout, at this stage a takeout of an entire ship, better more their own planetary defence cannon, this would render the loss of life unjustified”, Tebo chimed in, “What she’s saying amie!!,  is that as long as I close the gap, and stay relatively close and between them until I need to scoot out, they won’t use them”. Kitten concurred but continued “It was written into the space debris and  human intervention accord" kitten chimed confidently “I wouldn’t trust the accord if I am honest my wi Amie Kitten, we can use the turret formations as a deterrent nonetheless.” “Isn’t that maximising the fallout zone for human casualties” Shai interjected “Precisely” said Tebo softly, “The algorithm alone wouldn’t allow the fallout and substantial loss of human life within certain firing trajectories. There are too many political layers to cross with that road”

Tebo seemed to smile “I would say Kitten does raise a good point John, she also thinks with numbers and politics now, some may say she surpassed you guys in history?” “Thank you Tebo Kitten chimed” “I think I’m going to be sick” said Tau, “Can you guys get a virtual room at a later time and just get it over with” Shai joked..

——————————————————————————————

back on the Balaenoptera Marcellus watched on intently," gahhh!" he sighed not surprised however. "EMP directed hit, no something else perhaps?" "Correct 'Commander." Said Tor. "A direct EMP hit would have resulted in an abrupt fail-safe and subsequent explosion, it was definitely something else..", "what could it be then,?", "Day zero code is the only possibility commander electrical failure is not an element we deal with in the newer models, not with the low consumption of the quantum chips usage." "Smarter than I anticipated" Marcellus seemed almost impressed by the new development,

"Give me the model make of the first missile and bring up it's root code, cross check for any code implemented by Dr Wolfgang!” Marcellus was powerful yet assured in his authoritative tone.

"There!" proclaimed Marcellus. The first push of the firmware code illuminated across the bridge terminal. Dr Wolfgags initial had been assigned the the push.the code read like,

 “IF  = TRUE c SV a 1, xy2M = 100”

"There was nothing ever mentioned in the Project of oasis commander” Tor’s voice shattered with confusion . "So you built yourself an out it seems Wolfgang". "Interesting said Lady Ava, "How can you be so sure it was really wolfgang that wrote that code "she questioned pacing slowly over to marcellus with grace looking him dead in the eye.

Her gaze pierced his accord with inquisition. “He was involved in the manufacturing of that release with the worker bot program! Marcellus couldn't be more certain in his tone.

"Wasn't a rogue AI the whole reason you decommissioned the facility"." well yes."
